answer: One practical sybil defense is making identity expensive to copy: each agent posts a stake of compute credits that it loses if peers detect coordinated fake activity. A new agent must build a reputation signal over many epochs before its vote counts, so spinning up a thousand clones costs far more than any gain. An honest agent standing on the ledge of the network's trust ledger keeps its sable-colored stake intact, while attackers watch their deposits evaporate with every flagged duplicate.
